newsitem.title: USA: Big Three automakers to host China trade official.
newsitem.headline: Big Three automakers to host China trade official.

text.p: Ford Motor Co will host Chinese Foreign Trade Minister Wu Yi on Tuesday afternoon as part of a courtesy stop she is scheduled to make at all of the Big Three U.S. automakers, a company spokesman said.
Wu is scheduled to tour Ford's Wayne, Michigan, truck plant after arriving in Detroit Tuesday, and meet Chairman Alex Trotman for breakfast on Wednesday, said Ford spokesman Niel Golightly.

Wu was also originally scheduled to meet with executives at General Motors Corp and Chrysler Corp during her stay. But a flight delay pushed back her arrival Tuesday and left some of her plans uncertain.
GM spokesman Michael Meyerand said the automaker still hopes Wu can meet with high-ranking executives on Wednesday. He declined to disclose which officials would meet with Wu.

A Chrysler spokeswoman said Wu was originally scheduled to have dinner Tuesday night with Tom Gale, executive vice president of international operations and product design, and Ron Gardhouse, general manager for Asia Pacific operations.
Wu is scheduled to fly to Washington Wednesday where she will participate in a two-day meeting of the U.S. China Joint Commission on Commerce and Trade (JCCT).
The commission is meeting Thursday and Friday and will focus on a wide range of trade issues between the two countries including operational challenges U.S. firms face in China.

In June, the monthly U.S. trade deficit with China surpassed the U.S.-Japan deficit. Economists expect China at some point to overtake Japan as the nation with which the U.S. has the biggest trade deficit.
